body_markdown:
Ondas (ONDS) continues to expand its defense platform—this time by acquiring GATE Technologies and Bron Technologies.


The deal adds electronic safe-and-arm and fuzing technology.


In simple terms, these are the electronic systems that help ensure a munition remains safe during storage, transportation and launch—and arms or initiates only when the appropriate conditions are met.


GATE's technology is already integrated into 90+ weapon systems, including UAVs, loitering munitions, missiles and rockets.


[Ondas Acquires GATE Technologies and Bron Technologies, Expanding Precision-Strike Platform with Electronic Safe & Arm and Fuze Technology :: Ondas Inc. (ONDS)](https://ir.ondas.com/press-releases/detail/328/ondas-acquires-gate-technologies-and-bron-technologies)


##


The Numbers


-


$205M upfront consideration


-


Up to $185M additional performance-based earn-outs


-


GATE expected to generate ~$65M revenue in 2026


-


Management projects ~$180M revenue by 2028


-


Ondas expects $130M+ of cumulative adjusted EBITDA from the acquired businesses through 2028


ONDS is assembling more of the technology stack behind autonomous and precision-strike systems.


**Autonomous platforms → mission systems → communications → propulsion → precision strike → now electronic arming & fuzing**


GATE also brings something difficult to replicate quickly: technology already designed and qualified into dozens of weapons programs, while Bron adds Poland-based European manufacturing and certification capabilities.


There is a tradeoff.


This is another sizable acquisition for a company that has already been extremely active in M&A. Integration, capital allocation and delivering on management's aggressive growth expectations remain important things to watch.


But strategically, the direction is becoming clearer:


Ondas isn't trying to be just a drone company. It's trying to own more of the technology inside the autonomous weapons ecosystem.
